sections.section_name: Section A - Objective & Basic Biochemical Facts

questions.question_text: Which restriction endonuclease enzyme isolated from Escherichia coli leaves a characteristic $5'-GAATTC-3'$ palindromic sticky-ended cleavage pattern?
questions.answer: B) EcoRI

questions.question_text: What is the primary function of the enzyme DNA ligase in recombinant DNA technology?
options: A) To unwind the double helix structure
B) To catalyze the formation of phosphodiester bonds between adjacent DNA fragments
C) To synthesize RNA primers during replication
D) To hydrolyze internal peptide bonds in proteins
questions.answer: B) To catalyze the formation of phosphodiester bonds between adjacent DNA fragments

questions.question_text: Which of the following vectors is derived naturally from the bacteriophage lambda genome or M13 phages for cloning larger genomic fragments?
questions.answer: B) Bacteriophage Vector

questions.question_text: What is the name of the thermostable DNA polymerase extracted from the bacterium Thermus aquaticus used in Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR)?
options: A) E. coli DNA Polymerase I
questions.answer: B) Taq Polymerase

questions.question_text: Which technique is specifically utilized to separate DNA molecules based on their size and electrical charge using an agarose gel matrix?
questions.answer: B) Agarose Gel Electrophoresis

questions.question_text: The short segment of single-stranded DNA or RNA, about 20-30 nucleotides long, that is complementary to the target sequence in PCR is called a:
questions.answer: B) Primer

questions.question_text: Which genomic library construction component represents a collection of cDNA clones synthesized directly from cellular mRNA populations?
questions.answer: B) cDNA Library

questions.question_text: What type of ends are generated by restriction enzymes like SmaI that cut both strands of DNA at the exact same axis of symmetry?
questions.answer: B) Blunt ends

questions.question_text: Which gene transfer method utilizes microscopic gold or tungsten particles coated with DNA shot at high velocity into plant cells?
questions.answer: C) Biolistics (Gene Gun method)

questions.question_text: What is the structural role of the origin of replication ($ori$) sequence present on a plasmid vector?
options: A) It provides antibiotic resistance to the host
B) It controls plasmid copy number and initiates autonomous replication
C) It codes for restriction sites
D) It facilitates cell wall breakdown
questions.answer: B) It controls plasmid copy number and initiates autonomous replication

questions.question_text: Assertion (A): Plasmids are ideal cloning vectors because they replicate independently of the host chromosomal DNA. Reason (R): Plasmids lack any selectable marker genes, making selection dependent solely on cellular mass. Choose the correct option:
options: A) Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
B) Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
C) A is true, but R is false
D) A is false, but R is true
questions.answer: C) A is true, but R is false

questions.question_text: Which sequencing technique involves the incorporation of chain-terminating dideoxynucleotides (ddNTPs) labeled with fluorophores?
options: B) Sanger's Dideoxy Chain Termination Method
questions.answer: B) Sanger's Dideoxy Chain Termination Method

questions.question_text: What is the primary function of reverse transcriptase enzyme in genetic engineering pipelines?
options: A) Synthesizing DNA from an RNA template
B) Synthesizing RNA from a DNA template
questions.answer: A) Synthesizing DNA from an RNA template

questions.question_text: Which molecular scissors are characterized by recognizing specific palindromic sequences and cutting within or near their recognition sites?
questions.answer: B) Restriction Endonucleases

questions.question_text: What term is used to describe a DNA molecule that has been constructed outside of living cells by joining natural or synthetic DNA segments?
questions.answer: B) Recombinant DNA

questions.question_text: Which of the following host organisms is most commonly used for routine laboratory cloning procedures due to its well-mapped genetics and rapid growth rate?
questions.answer: B) Escherichia coli

questions.question_text: Assertion (A): The melting step in Polymerase Chain Reaction typically operates at high temperatures around $94^{\circ}\text{C}$ to $95^{\circ}\text{C}$. Reason (R): High temperatures break the hydrogen bonds holding complementary DNA strands together, yielding single-stranded templates. Choose the correct option:
options: A) Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
B) Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
C) A is true, but R is false
D) A is false, but R is true
questions.answer: A) Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A

questions.question_text: What is the function of ethidium bromide when utilized in agarose gel electrophoresis analysis?
options: A) To neutralize the electrical charge of DNA
B) To stain DNA fragments so they fluoresce under UV light
C) To act as a tracking dye during migration
questions.answer: B) To stain DNA fragments so they fluoresce under UV light

sections.section_name: Section B - Very Short Analytical Concepts

questions.question_text: Differentiate briefly between the functional role of select marker genes versus reporter genes inside an engineered host expression system. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Selectable markers (e.g., $amp^R$) allow the direct survival and isolation of transformants under selective antibiotic pressure. Reporter genes (e.g., $lacZ$, $GFP$) encode visually trackable phenotypes like color shifts or fluorescence to verify gene expression.

questions.question_text: Explain the significance of palindromic nucleotide sequences in restriction endonuclease digestion. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Palindromic sequences read identically in the $5' \to 3'$ direction on both complementary strands. Restriction enzymes recognize these symmetrical motifs to catalyze precise, uniform cleavages.

questions.question_text: Define the term 'Competent Cell' in the context of bacterial transformation protocols. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Competent cells are bacterial hosts treated chemically or physically (e.g., with calcium chloride or electroporation) to increase cell membrane permeability, allowing exogenous plasmid uptake.

questions.question_text: Distinguish between genomic DNA libraries and complementary DNA (cDNA) libraries. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: A genomic library contains total nuclear DNA representing all sequences, including introns. A cDNA library contains only expressed exon sequences derived from reverse-transcribed mRNA.

questions.question_text: State the structural purpose of adding dideoxynucleotides (ddNTPs) during Sanger sequencing reactions. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Lacking a $3'$-OH group, ddNTPs terminate chain elongation upon random incorporation into synthesized DNA strands, generating nested fragments for size-based reading.

sections.section_name: Section C - Short Explanatory & Procedural Steps

questions.question_text: Outline the crucial step-by-step procedural workflows required to execute a standard Southern Blotting hybridization technique to detect a specific target DNA fragment. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: First, separate DNA fragments using agarose gel electrophoresis, then denature the double strands. Transfer the single-stranded sheets onto a nylon membrane layout, fix them securely, and introduce radioactively labeled single-stranded DNA probes to map complementary fragments via autoradiography.

questions.question_text: Describe the three fundamental thermal cycles involved in each round of Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) amplification. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: PCR cycles begin with denaturation at $95^{\circ}\text{C}$ to separate strands. Next, annealing at $50-65^{\circ}\text{C}$ allows primers to bind target sites. Finally, extension at $72^{\circ}\text{C}$ enables Taq polymerase to synthesize new complementary strands.

questions.question_text: Explain the mechanism of insertional inactivation using the $lacZ$ gene for blue-white colony screening. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Inserting foreign DNA into the $lacZ$ gene disrupts $\alpha$-peptide production, rendering recombinant colonies white on X-gal plates. Non-recombinant colonies retain functional $\beta$-galactosidase activity, producing a distinct blue color.

questions.question_text: Detail how Agrobacterium tumefaciens naturally infects plant cells to transfer foreign genes, serving as a natural vector. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Agrobacterium transfers its tumor-inducing (Ti) plasmid T-DNA segment into the plant host genome following plant wounding signals. Genetic engineers replace oncogenic genes with desirable traits for stable plant transformation.

questions.question_text: Explain the process and purpose of alkaline phosphatase treatment on linearized vector DNA prior to ligation. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Alkaline phosphatase removes $5'$-phosphate groups from linearized vectors, preventing self-ligation loops. This enzymatic step drastically increases recombinant cloning efficiency by forcing vector-insert hybrid formations.

questions.question_text: Read the following bioprocess case context: A manufacturing pipeline utilizes a continuous-stirred tank bioreactor to express a recombinant therapeutic protein. Kinetic logs indicate the specific growth rate $\mu$ drops sharply as biomass density $X$ hits a saturation point of $45\text{ g/L}$ due to toxic secondary metabolite accumulation. Calculate the critical dilution rate $D$ required to maintain steady-state biomass equilibrium assuming Monod kinetics configurations match $\mu = \mu_{\max} \frac{S}{K_s + S}$. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: At a steady-state chemostat layout, the specific growth rate equals the operational dilution rate ($D = \mu$). To maintain cellular biomass balance without wash-out, the operator must tune feed input metrics so $D$ matches $\mu$. Substituting parameters secures stable long-term equilibrium lines where substrate replenishment perfectly matches metabolite dilution rates.

questions.question_text: Analyze an electrophoresis gel profiling data report: Lane 1 contains uncut circular plasmid DNA, Lane 2 contains plasmid digested with a single-cut restriction enzyme, and Lane 3 shows double-digestion fragments yielding sizes of $2.5\text{ kb}$ and $1.0\text{ kb}$. Deduce the total plasmid size and explain why supercoiled circular DNA migrates faster than linear forms. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: The total plasmid size is $3.5\text{ kb}$ ($2.5 + 1.0$). Supercoiled circular DNA migrates faster through agarose gels than linear DNA because its compact, tightly wound conformation experiences significantly less frictional drag against the gel matrix pores during electrical migration.

questions.question_text: Review a molecular diagnostics scenario: A clinical laboratory runs a PCR test for an infectious pathogen. After 35 thermal cycles, amplification curves remain completely flat, but positive control wells show strong signals. Evaluate potential procedural failures in the master mix or template preparation. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: Flat amplification curves alongside a valid positive control indicate template failure or inhibitory compounds in the patient sample. Potential issues include degraded target DNA, insufficient primer binding due to mutations, or carryover contaminants like phenol/ethanol inhibiting Taq polymerase activity.

sections.section_name: Section E - Long-Form Structural & Genetic Models

questions.question_text: Deconstruct the structural mapping configuration of the landmark cloning vector pBR322. Detail the exact spatial parameters and orientations of the origin of replication ($ori$), the $rop$ gene element, and the dual antibiotic resistance genes explaining the insertional inactivation screening mechanism. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: The pBR322 plasmid layout contains an $ori$ region for autonomous replication and a $rop$ gene coding for copy-number control proteins. It features two selectable markers: the ampicillin resistance gene ($amp^R$) and the tetracycline resistance gene ($tet^R$). Cloning an external DNA fragment into the unique BamHI site located inside the $tet^R$ gene disrupts its reading frame. This insertional inactivation yields transformants that are ampicillin-resistant but tetracycline-sensitive, facilitating clear phenotypic screening.

questions.question_text: Provide an extensive structural breakdown of the Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) technique. Describe the roles of primers, Taq DNA polymerase, thermal cycling parameters, and list two major practical applications in genomic research and clinical diagnostics. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: PCR amplifies target DNA exponentially via three repeated thermal phases: denaturation ($95^{\circ}\text{C}$), primer annealing ($50-65^{\circ}\text{C}$), and extension ($72^{\circ}\text{C}$). Primers define the specific region to amplify, while thermostable Taq polymerase withstands high heat cycles. Practical applications include forensic DNA fingerprinting and early prenatal screening for genetic disorders.

questions.question_text: Examine the architectural layout and operational workflow of a recombinant gene expression system utilizing Escherichia coli. Explain transcription induction via the lac operon promoter, translation control metrics, and downstream isolation strategies to recover pure intracellular proteins. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: Expression in E. coli utilizes strong promoters like lac or tac, inducible by IPTG to drive target gene transcription. Translational efficiency is optimized via Shine-Dalgarno ribosome binding sites. Following fermentation, cells are harvested and lysed mechanically. Intracellular recombinant proteins are recovered using affinity chromatography, leveraging engineered polyhistidine tags for high-purity downstream isolation.
